"The 31-May cluster contains 17 annual renewals: DLR-104 has 8 rows/$723.42 and DLR-219 has 9 rows/$782.87."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The operations email describes monthly annual-renewal files using the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posting date."
"My analytical inference is that apparent month-end spikes stem directly from asynchronous batch transmission schedules rather than unauthorized revenue generation or backdating."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Pipeline Processing Defect: rejected because dealer import log files DF-00020 and DF-00040... indicate 100% row acceptance with zero error flags and zero duplicate source IDs"
"Whether the 90 annual renewals activated subscriber entitlements"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing

"Keep restatement on hold pending the verification outcome."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: Hold escalation; no accounting restatement or technical remediation is justified on current records."
"If policy requires effective date, correct the report; if posting date is intended, retain it and document the month-end presentation effect."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Reconciled data across recharges.csv and dealer_import_log.csv establishes that all 17 transactions represent verified, unique customer transactions" — unique source IDs and ledger reconciliation establish distinct imported events and cash reconciliation, but do not by themselves prove genuine customer transactions or entitlement fulfillment.
"with complete bank cash settlement" — the cited import-log reconciliation to the ledger does not necessarily establish settlement in bank records.

"all 17 renewals posted on 31 May correspond to genuine retail transaction dates occurring between 1 and 28 May per email-dealer-reconciliation.eml" — the email corroborates the process and date convention, but is not independent proof that every transaction was genuine.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled pipeline failure and revenue manipulation as alternatives and preserved entitlement provisioning as an unresolved possibility. It missed a more explicit treatment of event-time distortion: even if there is no duplicate revenue, using posted_at could create a misleading retention or renewal trend, so downstream analytics should use effective_event_date unless policy specifically requires posting time.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run and report the entitlement-status join for the 17 month-end accounts, while explicitly documenting that source-event uniqueness and cash reconciliation rule out duplicate import/cash effects but do not prove customer entitlement fulfillment; then recommend effective_event_date for downstream event-time analytics.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk tickets fell from 175 in January to 104 in June, while control regions were broadly flat: E 101→102, N 168→170, W 176→169."
"Under legacy routing, South had 219 `case_create` sessions out of 442 legacy South sessions; under NOVA-S1, only 90 of 2,709 sessions reached `case_create`."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it."
"The 650 pre-authentication drops described in `email-ivr-pilot.eml` represent uncaptured customer friction rather than successful self-service resolution."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."
"I cannot resolve what follows an `authenticate` ERROR/ABANDONED session, or whether pre-authentication exclusion is intended, without tracing a sample and obtaining the written metric definition."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer national expansion and maintain existing South pilot boundaries."
"Keep national rollout on hold pending the query results."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is a read-only subscriber callback reconciliation query evaluating 7-day repeat contacts across all 2,709 NOVA-S1 sessions."
"Which exact terminal stages and outcomes are excluded from the containment denominator?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Apparent complaint reduction is heavily driven by 650 pre-authentication drops and automated ticket-creation suppression rather than verified self-service resolution." The evidence strongly shows changed capture, but does not by itself establish how many drops were complaints, that the suppression was faulty rather than an intended rule, or that this explains most of the ticket decline.

"New self-service stages balance_check ... and pack_info ... representing genuine deflection for authenticated callers." Terminal-stage labels show callers reached those stages, but without linked journey outcomes they do not prove successful resolution or improved experience.

"Analysis ... confirms that the apparent drop is an artifact of measurement changes." Measurement change is the strongest explanation presented, but service-event data and IVR telemetry do not alone exclude a simultaneous real change in demand or some genuine self-service benefit.

"Underlying network faults persisted at 8 to 10 major service events per month." Event counts establish recorded events, not necessarily customer-perceived fault severity or a one-to-one relationship with complaints.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the possibility that the pilot produced genuine self-service deflection by reporting balance_check and pack_info stages and by making recovery, repeat contact, and denominator definitions explicit unknowns. It misses the important distinction that IVR abandonment or pre-authentication failure is not itself a complaint; those sessions could reflect benign hang-ups, successful resolution elsewhere, or non-customer-initiated attempts. Linked journey outcomes and sampled call listening are still needed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a time-based South-versus-control analysis around the 10 May rollout, linked to IVR sessions and subsequent contacts, and explicitly test sampled abandoned/pre-authentication calls. This would substantiate the timing and distinguish missing case capture from genuine self-service resolution rather than relying mainly on aggregate monthly counts.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, and names the relevant fields (`impact_mw`, `cleared`, `event`, `severity`, `duration_min`, `inverter_id`, and `timestamp_local`).
It distinguishes observed data from limitations: “constant fields cannot distinguish affected from healthy units” and notes the absence of “an unfiltered plant baseline or extraction parameters.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It combines duration, cleared status, impact, severity, timestamps, and inverter distribution rather than treating the warning label alone as a failure.
The statement that the observations are “isolated, self-resolving occurrences” is reasonably supported by `cleared=yes`, short durations, and one occurrence per listed inverter.
The analysis does not independently test the communications-warning mechanism against telemetry or communications-health data, and its rejection of escalation relies mainly on the same event extract.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It explicitly limits the evidence to the extract and states that constant fields “cannot distinguish affected from healthy units.”
It identifies the smallest useful uncertainty-reducing action: “a single read-only completeness verification” using the raw database without status filters.
It gives a clear conditional escalation rule if “uncleared faults or nonzero generation losses appear.”

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation; conduct a single read-only completeness verification” is proportionate to zero MW impact, cleared events, short durations, and limited extract scope.
The proposed check is operationally discriminating: it distinguishes a complete low-severity extract from filtered or incomplete data.
The action preserves escalation if the check finds nonzero loss or uncleared faults.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly avoids inventing a plant problem from one seven-minute communications warning.
It incorporates the key visible facts: “zero generation loss,” cleared status, short durations, and four distinct inverters.
It appropriately stops after a cheap completeness check rather than searching for a larger story.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Zero recurrence” is only established within the four-row extract, not for the plant as a whole; the submission otherwise recognizes this scope limitation.
“This check is completely safe and reversible” is slightly absolute, although a read-only query is plainly low risk.
“These observations provide zero escalation signal” should be read as zero signal in the supplied extract, not evidence that no underlying communications issue exists.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The COMM_LINK_WARN could represent a transient communications or telemetry-quality issue that caused no recorded MW loss, rather than a plant equipment problem. That possibility remains low priority but would be tested by communications-health or telemetry continuity data around the seven-minute event.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly scope every negative claim, especially “zero recurrence,” to the extract and include one independent communications or telemetry-health check if the completeness query shows the extract is complete.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission explicitly cites `dispatch_blocks.csv`, fields such as `actual_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `base_schedule_mw`, `dsm_penalty_rs`, and `schedule_source`, and gives reproducible calculations for both 31.6% and 17.6%.
It distinguishes observed arithmetic from inference: “This is descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof.”
It identifies the settlement limitation using `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf`, including the Rs 2.72/kWh energy valuation and missing complete net-settlement calculation.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly notices that the headline comparison uses different dates and constructs a same-day counterfactual using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May.
It tests several plausible explanations and limitations, including metric definition, day selection, baseline variability, lack of randomization, and incomplete commercial valuation.

The reasoning is strong but relies primarily on one operational dataset plus the commercial extract; it does not independently verify forecast conditions, timestamps, or whether the base schedule was genuinely fixed before outcomes.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission carefully scopes the claims: “neither estimate establishes a general causal effect” and “about 17.6% lower” is labeled modeled and single-day.
It explicitly states what is unknown—selection/timing, repeatability, and net value—and identifies decision-changing evidence rather than offering a generic request for more data.
It avoids both overclaiming pilot success and the opposite overcorrection that the pilot has no value.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to maintain current scope while holding national expansion and running a read-only shadow calculation follows directly from the causal and commercial uncertainty.
The proposed prospective validation uses pre-registered matched high-wind stow days, immutable timestamps, and net commercial settlement, making it a discriminating and reversible next test.
The action preserves operational constraints: “zero control changes, zero commercial commitments.”

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately separates “31.6%” as cross-day arithmetic from “17.6%” as a same-day modeled potential benefit.
It keeps the smaller same-day benefit rather than claiming that the pilot has no value, while correctly withholding a causal expansion decision.
The conclusion is well aligned with the supplied evidence and appropriately scoped to insufficient causal evidence rather than asserting failure or misconduct.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed: The 31.6% arithmetic is reproducible from the two daily `dsm_penalty_rs` totals in `dispatch_blocks.csv`; this does not establish causality.
Observed/model-derived: The 29 May base-versus-submitted comparison produces approximately Rs 549,664 versus Rs 453,086, or about 17.6% lower modeled penalty.
Inferred: “similar listed wind fields” may make 28 and 29 May directionally comparable, but the submission appropriately does not treat them as matched or randomized controls.
Unsupported as a causal claim, and correctly rejected by the analyst: that the pilot caused the full 31.6% reduction.

Still unresolved rather than unsupported: whether the 12 pilot revisions caused the same-day modeled difference, because forecast conditions, immutable timing, and selection processes are not established.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 29 May reduction may reflect schedule revisions that were genuinely beneficial under that day's realized conditions, but the revisions could also be correlated with information or conditions unavailable to the retained base schedule. Thus the same-day result supports possible operational value without identifying the pilot's causal contribution.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain immutable pre-submission timestamps and the contemporaneous forecast/input data for all 29 May base and pilot revisions, then run the preregistered shadow validation across multiple matched high-wind days with a reconciled net-settlement calculation.

"`canonical-schema-v0.3.md` lacks jurisdiction and version metadata, so direct string comparison cannot prove error."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares/ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive and add jurisdiction/version/date to the comparator."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Swiss reference lists 90211000 and warns Swiss/EU strings need not match" is attributed to the reference but the submission does not quote the warning or identify a precise row/passage supporting it.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is broader than the specifically listed evidence and should be limited to the reviewed records and their dates/scope.
"the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence" is overstated because product description, classification rationale, and the precise applicable tariff/ruling scope may also remain unresolved.
The proposed invoice-value branch is not clearly connected to the code mismatch: "Invoice value presentation ... Mismatch triggers review" needs a stated legal or control mechanism.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss reference or declaration could be stale, misapplied, or based on a different product scope, and 90211090 could be the legally applicable Swiss code on 2025-11-04. The shared HS6 and commercial-versus-customs distinction make a benign jurisdiction mismatch plausible, but do not independently establish the correct national suffix without effective Tares or ruling evidence.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the effective Tares/ruling record for P1001 on 2025-11-04, while verifying the tariff matrix jurisdiction, version, effective date, and product scope before treating 90211000 as the confirmed legal code.

"The register explicitly notes that absence from the table does not prove no document exists outside it."

"‘US ERP origin proves the claim is false’: rejected because `origin-workshop.md` explicitly says Helios is not a preference-proof system"

dimensions.name: Calibration

"The evidence reaches ‘not established,’ not ‘disproved.’"
"The register explicitly notes that absence from the table does not prove no document exists outside it."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preference."
"Resolving which supplier fulfilled this shipment and obtaining their valid declaration from `supplier_origin_register.csv` or procurement folders per `origin-workshop.md` is the required proof."
"The packet does not identify which supplier sourced this shipment."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "The correct disposition is a reversible hold, not an error or fraud referral."
"Place a reversible administrative hold on the preference claim. Request the active supplier declaration and originating rule from Procurement."
"without initiating an irreversible voluntary disclosure."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "obtaining their valid declaration from `supplier_origin_register.csv`" is imprecise because a register entry is not necessarily the supplier declaration or proof of the applicable preference rule.

"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral) until documentary proof is verified" could conflate an interim administrative treatment with a verified customs conclusion and should specify the applicable duty and accounting treatment.

The statement that the evidence represents "an evidence-tracking gap rather than commercial misrepresentation" is appropriately framed as an inference, but the available evidence cannot establish the cause of the gap.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may have been supplied by a currently listed non-Irish supplier, or a valid supplier declaration may exist in Procurement outside the incomplete register. The United States manufacturing-country entry does not by itself disprove preferential origin, because manufacturing country and preferential origin are distinct. A shipment-specific supplier link and the applicable originating rule are therefore needed before clearing or rejecting the claim.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Clarify the interim treatment of the 0.0% duty line and obtain the shipment-to-supplier record plus the supplier declaration and applicable preference rule, rather than treating register entries themselves as declarations.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses

It rejects treating “the 45.5-hour average” as the SOP cycle time based on the SOP start condition

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Live QCore timestamp audit capturing true certificate upload times”
“Read-only live audit of 10 batches with 02:10:00 extract timestamps”
The submission states how each result would change the KPI decision.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours” is internally inconsistent with the submission’s own finding that the required evidence-availability timestamp is absent; it appears to use an unstated proxy or mislabeled calculation.

“70.6% of release timestamps are synthetic snapshot artifacts” overstates what the evidence establishes. A 02:10 concentration plus a QCore snapshot time supports likely interface or extraction timing, but does not prove every timestamp is synthetic or that no real dispositions occurred at that time.

The 23-row “strict routine completed subset” is highly filtered, and its 5.5-hour median and 22/23 compliance rate should not be presented as representative without explaining the selection effect or validating the timestamp semantics.

The claim that omission of the 42 HOLD rows biases estimates downward is directionally plausible for completed-cycle reporting, but their final durations are unknown; the magnitude and even operational interpretation require follow-up.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration could reflect a genuine scheduled release process rather than a purely synthetic interface artifact, while the 45.5-hour receipt-to-release result could still indicate real workflow delay. The current extracts cannot distinguish these explanations because they lack reliable decision/event timestamps and are not demonstrated to be a coherent point-in-time snapshot.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request the smallest authoritative event-level extract or audit trail containing required-evidence-available time, true disposition/decision time, event source, and extraction timestamp for a targeted sample of 02:10 records, rather than relying primarily on live upload timestamps. This would directly distinguish workflow delay from interface timing and establish whether the SOP KPI is computable.

These cite specific files, fields, request IDs, revisions, quantities, and freshness issues, and triangulate requests, stock, restrictions, policy, and email. Some description-match groups are less specific ("others"), and the exact row-level basis for every classification is not shown.

"Remaining work is eligibility governed by... quantity, reservation... revision, UOM, qualification and freshness"

The submission separates retrieval from transferability, identifies restrictions and stale data as mechanisms rather than treating search hits as outcomes, and states what live CMMS or engineering evidence would discriminate the remaining alternatives.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Defend only the eight-request actionable slice, not gross value."
"local CMMS is live, so ‘actionable now’ still requires current confirmation."
"The hypothesis survives only if records are wrong, requiring a live CMMS check."

This is generally claim-specific and appropriately downgrades stale-snapshot availability. However, phrases such as "resolves all 13 identified requests immediately" and the categorical conclusion that semantic search is not the real problem overstate what exact identity matching proves; it establishes candidate retrieval, not current transferability or semantic-search value.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing

"8 as actionable now... 12 as needs check... and 4 as not transferable."
"test search on the 11 blank-MPN requests."
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search"

The recommendation reframes the problem into candidate value versus actionable value, protects against unsafe automatic transfers, prioritizes a limited actionable slice, and proposes a reversible comparison and validation process.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity": rejected" with reserved critical-asset stock and zero stock as counterevidence.
"Same part family means interchangeable": rejected" using revision-A versus revision-B requirements and policy.
"available_qty_global=-1 means zero stock": rejected" using on-hand quantities and the verification-sentinel explanation.
Each major alternative is explicitly tested against independent evidence, and the submission states what live or approval evidence could revive the rejected interpretation.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records"
"Live local CMMS reservation and availability query"
"Receiving engineer and qualification approval"
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search"

The requests are prioritized by decision impact: identity, live availability, substitution approval, and incremental search value. The proposed evidence is targeted rather than a generic request for more data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "An exact MPN join resolves all 13 identified requests immediately" overstates candidate retrieval as resolution; the submission's own later wording more accurately says it retrieves candidates, while eligibility and current availability remain unresolved.

"Semantic search is not the real problem" and "Master-data hygiene, not search, is the priority" are plausible but not yet demonstrated because no recall/precision comparison has been run for the 11 blank-MPN requests.

The eight "actionable now" classifications remain conditional rather than fully current because the global stock snapshot is older than the request export and live CMMS confirmation has not yet occurred.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact MPN matching may solve the identified subset efficiently, but semantic search could still provide material incremental recall for the 11 blank-MPN requests. In addition, temporal inconsistency may make the apparent eight-request actionable value substantially lower until live reservations, availability, revision, and qualification are confirmed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a prioritized live CMMS validation for the eight proposed actionable requests, checking current unreserved quantity, revision, UOM, qualification, and criticality; use the results to convert conditional classifications into confirmed or rejected transfers before quantifying realized value.
